data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash -x
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --time=00:30:00
#   --partition=batch
#   --output=run.out
#   --error=run.err

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=30m
#flux: --output=run.out
#flux: --error=run.err

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=batch
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-node=4 (explicit per-node placement)
# Flux does not have a universally portable batch directive for tasks-per-node.
# Performance implication: if the job were to span multiple nodes, rank placement might differ; here we force -N 1 to preserve intent.

export LD_PRELOAD=$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_def.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_avx2.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_lp64.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_thread.so:$EBROOTIMKL/lib/intel64/libiomp5.so

export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/p/project/ccstma/cstma000/pySDC

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, use flux-run to launch 4 ranks.
flux run -n 4 -c 1 python pySDC_with_PETSc.py 1

touch ready

reasons: The original Slurm job specified a partition (`--partition=batch`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

srun python pySDC_with_PETSc.py 1
touch ready
